subjects.label: Characters, families and succession
subjects.description: The ruling family as a system: heirs and succession, marriages and kidnapped relatives, relationships between named characters, the portraits that tell them apart and whether you can make your own dynasty rather than pick a preset one; it does not cover the plot of a single event or the factions as nations.

subjects.label: Orders and the action limit per turn
subjects.description: The pool of orders that caps how many units and actions you can spend each turn, whether it is a clever innovation or a pointless restriction; it does not cover combat or movement rules in general.

subjects.label: Story events and event pop-ups
subjects.description: The random narrative events and event chains that interrupt each turn, whether their choices matter, whether they repeat across playthroughs and whether the pop-ups engage or merely interrupt; it does not cover the historical setting or the family system as such.

subjects.label: Measured against Civilization and Crusader Kings
subjects.description: Explicit comparison with Sid Meier's Civilization or Crusader Kings, as a Civ-killer, a Civ clone, Civ 4.5, the Civ 6 that should have been or a hybrid of the two; it does not cover 4X genre labels that name no specific game.

subjects.label: The ancient world and historical fidelity
subjects.description: The ancient Mediterranean as a setting, real figures such as Hypatia and Herodotus, learning history from it and whether the game is true to the period or revises it; it does not cover which nations are missing or how long the era lasts.

subjects.label: Which nations and how far in time
subjects.description: The scope of the roster and the timeline: wishes for India, Armenia or later ages and techs, and whether the narrow era ends too soon or is exactly the focus wanted; it does not cover map count or the setting's authenticity.

subjects.label: Late-game slowdown
subjects.description: The game degrading as the turn count climbs, with next-turn waits that stretch out past turn 100 or 200 and crashes late in a campaign even on capable hardware; it does not cover general optimisation complaints with no turn count behind them.

subjects.label: The AI opponent
subjects.description: How the computer players and tribes behave: whether the AI is a real challenge, whether it cheats or has an unfair edge, tribes spawning units and turning hostile, and the monthly AI work on the test branch; it does not cover difficulty settings in the abstract.

subjects.label: One more turn
subjects.description: The pull of the next turn: sitting down for a couple of turns and finding it is dawn, twenty minutes before work, a time-eater and a genuine addiction; it does not cover the mood or tension of play itself.

subjects.label: Pace of play
subjects.description: How slowly a game unfolds by design: sluggish opening, turns that drag even at maximum speed, not a game for anyone who wants a quick match; it does not cover technical lag or how many hours the game lasts.
